metadata.description: Post-core feature backlog for PhotoBlaze. These ship AFTER the core viewer is stable (roadmap Phases 0-3: window, decode-to-fit, prefetch ring, hold-to-blaze). Every task obeys the prime directive (faster or perf-neutral) and the project's TDD rules: pure logic isolated and unit-tested, GPU work behind the Renderer seam, golden-image tests for visuals. Shared infrastructure is factored out so it is built once: a per-photo ViewTransform (rotation + zoom + scaling mode), a translucent HUD/overlay layer, and a central configurable action/keymap.

tasks.title: Windows: single-instance window reuse + Explorer multi-select as one playlist
tasks.description: Make Windows match the macOS open idiom (LaunchServices already gives the Mac one instance + one openURLs batch). Today each Explorer double-click/Open spawns a FULL new process (decode pool + resident VRAM ring each; settings.toml write races), and multi-select Open invokes one process per file (Explorer blocks >15 selections by default — MultipleInvokePromptMinimum — so the blast radius is capped at ~15 processes, but that is still bad). Plan: (a) accept multiple CLI path args -> classify_inputs (the Vec<PathBuf> -> LaunchInput::Files machinery already serves drag-drop/picker); (b) MultiSelectModel=Player on the ProgID (a REG_SZ value written by the existing per-user HKCU self-registration in default_app.rs — NOT an MSI component; WiX/MSI was retired when Velopack shipped, see archived task #51/#50) so a multi-select arrives as ONE invocation; (c) single-instance: named mutex, loser forwards its paths via WM_COPYDATA to the running instance (-> open_paths -> open_plan) and exits, winner comes to front (AllowSetForegroundWindow) — this also merges the multiple invocations Explorer emits when a huge selection overflows the ~32K command line. Compare-two-photos is NOT this task: thats #43 (or a future explicit File > New Window command, which the mutex design must not preclude — e.g. a --new-window flag bypass). MSIX/Store evaluation moved out to decisions.md (revisit only if monetizing). Windows machine required.
tasks.details: Milestone C (ADR-018). Set-default: a button/hotkey opens ms-settings:defaultapps (or the Default Programs UI), since Windows forbids silent default seizure. Single-instance (optional): forward a newly-opened path to the running window (named pipe / mutex) instead of spawning a second window - nicer for double-click bursts; defer if it complicates the hot path. A modern Win11 inline folder verb would need an IExplorerCommand COM handler - only pursue if the 'Show more options' legacy verb from Task 13 feels inadequate. MSIX/Store: revisit only when charging money - it buys discovery + MS-managed signing/updates but costs the cheap folder verb and adds container friction.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual: 'Set as default' opens the right Settings page; a second launch with single-instance adopts the new photo in the existing window. MSIX evaluation deferred.

subtasks.title: Single-instance mutex + WM_COPYDATA forward
subtasks.description: DONE: pb-app/src/single_instance.rs. Named mutex (Local\PhotoBlaze.SingleInstance) elects a primary; a secondary absolutizes its paths, forwards them via WM_COPYDATA to the primary's message-only window, grants foreground (AllowSetForegroundWindow), and exits before any GPU/decode setup. Primary runs the IPC receiver on a background thread, wakes the winit loop via EventLoopProxy, and opens forwarded paths through open_input (same path as drag-drop). --new-window skips election. Retry loop covers the primary-still-starting race.

tasks.description: DETAILED PLAN: .taskmaster/docs/ai-descriptions-plan.md (2026-07-03; HUD/panel target revised 2026-07-05 by task #54). Describe the current image with a vision model. Trigger: `D` (rebindable; menu + context menu), result overlaid where the detailed info panel goes; optional auto-describe when the user PARKS on an image >500 ms (EAGER_PREP_DELAY pattern) — cancelled on advance (generation counter), results cached RAM-only per image (meta_cache pattern), dropped on exit. Auto mode is an opt-in toggle: fine by construction on the Apple on-device backend, but a configured endpoint could be remote, and passive sends must be a deliberate choice. Two backends behind one core-owned seam/policy: (1) macOS 27+ Foundation Models framework (on-device, image input, ships with the OS); (2) an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint (LM Studio / llama.cpp / Ollama — Qwen3-VL-8B or 27B-class on an RTX 5090) for Windows and power users. One-shot v1 (streaming later if slow; expected 1–5 s). Prompt built in core so both backends match: salient EXIF (capture time, camera/lens, raw GPS coords — offline reverse-geocoder is a LATER upgrade), filename + parent folder; all context framed as UNVERIFIED (trust-the-pixels instruction — hallucination guard) with epoch-default junk dates filtered out. Custom prompt template = advanced, settings.toml-only in v1 ({filename}/{folder}/{datetime}/{location}/{camera} placeholders). Optional TTS via CoreEffect::Speak — AVSpeechSynthesizer / Windows.Media.SpeechSynthesis, offline system voices, speech stops on navigation. New 'AI Descriptions' settings section (own tab on macOS): backend picker (Auto/Apple/Local), endpoint URL + model, auto-describe toggle, speak-aloud toggle. Privacy (ADR-018): never cloud, RAM-only, no sidecars/caches on disk; the endpoint URL + toggles are the only persisted config. v1 scope: on-disk stills (archive entries punted like Delete). Interim HUD note: pb-hud font fallback helps the current paragraph renderer and non-Latin EXIF/text values, but task #54 makes Description/Ask a rich panel with selectable/copyable text; the HUD is not the final rich-text surface. Additions from final discussion: 'Speak descriptions' is ALSO a menu toggle (Image menu, Mute-Live-Photo-Audio pattern, MenuState checkbox); the AI Descriptions settings section carries a short privacy blurb (custom endpoint = your images upload to that URL, incl. auto-describe — keep it local/trusted; online services may retain/train on images). || WWDC26 CONFIRMED (2026-07-04, https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2026/241/): FM image input is NEW in the 2026 release (macOS 27) — on-device, ships with the OS, no download/setup; API is session.respond { PROMPT; Attachment(x) } where x = NSImage/CGImage/CIImage/CVPixelBuffer/file-URL, any size/aspect. VQA confirmed — the model answers ARBITRARY user questions about an image, not just captions (new subtask 9). WARNING: the 2M-first-time-downloads cap the owner saw is on PRIVATE CLOUD COMPUTE (the cloud escalation tier), NOT the free on-device model; and PCC is CLOUD, so per ADR-018 (never cloud by our hand) we request the ON-DEVICE model ONLY and never PCC — the cap does not constrain us. 3rd-party server models (Anthropic/Google) also plug into the FM framework, billed per-token — not our path. tasks.title: Vendor-patch wgpu-hal: presentsWithTransaction during window-mode transitions (flash-free resize, MTKView-grade)
tasks.description: Make the fullscreen-toggle / resize composite pixel-perfect on macOS. Today's mitigation (2026-07-04) is benign-not-atomic: layerContentsPlacement=.center + contentsGravity on the canvas view means the one racy composite ({new bounds, previous drawable} — wgpu presents out-of-band from the CA transaction that moves the bounds) shows UNSCALED stale content for <=1 frame instead of a stretch. The atomic fix is Apple's presentsWithTransaction (what MTKView flips on during live resize). wgpu-hal 22's Metal backend ALREADY implements the correct present branch (Surface.present_with_transaction pub field; present does commit -> wait_until_scheduled -> drawable.present(); the field's own doc comment cites resize-sensitive UI apps) — but wgpu 22 gives no safe way to SET it: Surface::as_hal hands out only a shared ref, there's no creation-time knob, and configure() re-asserts the flag onto the layer every resize (so flipping the CAMetalLayer property from Swift is useless). PLAN: (1) vendor wgpu-hal 22.0 with a ~20-line patch — interior-mutable flag (AtomicBool) + set_present_with_transaction(&self) — wired via [patch.crates-io] like the sevenz-rust2 precedent; (2) pb-render seam Renderer::set_present_with_transaction(bool) reaching the hal surface through Surface::as_hal; (3) flip it ON only around window-mode transitions (and optionally during live resize), OFF otherwise — presentsWithTransaction costs a main-thread waitUntilScheduled block per present, which MTKView itself only tolerates while resizing; the photo hot path (hold-to-blaze) never resizes, keypress->photon untouched; (4) owner drives the upstream PR against wgpu trunk — NOTE trunk's Metal backend was rewritten on objc2 in 23+, so the trunk patch is the same concept but different code; a hal-level setter is the least-bikesheddable API shape. When the eventual egui/wgpu upgrade train moves off 22, the vendored patch drops (if merged) or re-rolls. Payoff is polish: the remaining <=1-frame unscaled reveal on F-toggles/live-resize becomes zero-artifact.

tasks.title: macOS window toolbar — nav + view/panel affordances (NSToolbar)
tasks.description: Owner idea (2026-07-05): a togglable toolbar for mouse-driven control — next/previous/random navigation buttons, toggles for the Inspector and folder-tree panels, and other frequently-used actions (rotate? delete? open?). This is a discoverability/mouse-affordance layer on top of the existing keyboard-driven core, not a new set of behaviors — every button should just fire an existing Action/PanelAction (Next/Previous/Random, ShowInspectorTab, ToggleTree, TogglePanels, etc.) through the same CoreEvent path a keypress uses today. Tension to resolve with the owner before implementation: CLAUDE.md's prime directive is a borderless, chrome-less window — an always-visible toolbar would contradict that, so 'togglable' likely means hidden by default and revealed on demand (a hotkey, and/or reveal-on-mouse-move-to-edge like fullscreen video players), never persistent chrome that eats into the fit-to-screen image area.

tasks.title: Smoother hold-to-pan / hold-to-zoom — gentler acceleration curve
tasks.description: Owner feel note (2026-07-09): holding the pan/zoom keys accelerates too aggressively and doesn't feel smooth — want a slower, gentler ramp with smoother motion. The hold-to-view loop is AppCore::apply_view_holds (crates/pb-app-core/src/app_core_impl.rs:5642), driven by the tuning constants in crates/pb-app-core/src/engine.rs: zoom e-folding rate ramps ZOOM_MIN_RATE 0.5 -> ZOOM_MAX_RATE 2.5 over ZOOM_RAMP_SECS 0.7 (exp() applied multiplicatively about center); pan speed ramps PAN_MIN_SPEED 450 -> PAN_MAX_SPEED 3200 px/s over PAN_RAMP_SECS 0.7. Both are already time-based (frame-rate independent, dt-clamped to 0.1s) so 'smoother' here means the FEEL of the ramp, not a timing bug. Two levers: (a) TUNING — lower the max rate/speed and/or lengthen the ramp so it starts and stays gentler (e.g. PAN_MAX ~1800-2400, ZOOM_MAX ~1.5-2.0, RAMP ~1.0-1.2s), a one-file constant change; (b) CURVE SHAPE — the ramp is currently LINEAR in t (min + (max-min)*(t/ramp)); an ease-in (smoothstep / t^2) keeps fine control longer at the start before building speed, which reads as 'smoother'. Optional stretch: a short release ease-out / inertia so motion doesn't stop dead on key-up. Shared-core feel change (helps macOS + Linux too), surfaced while testing on Windows; keep it a measured, owner-in-the-loop tuning pass, not a blind edit.
tasks.details: Scope options, cheapest first: (1) Retune the six constants (ZOOM_MIN/MAX_RATE, ZOOM_RAMP_SECS, PAN_MIN/MAX_SPEED, PAN_RAMP_SECS) for a gentler start and lower top speed — pure constant edit in engine.rs, no logic change. (2) Swap the linear ramp for an ease-in in apply_view_holds: factor the shared 'min + (max-min) * shape(t/ramp)' into a small pure helper (e.g. ease_in(u)=u*u or smoothstep) so zoom and pan share one curve and it's unit-testable (assert monotonic, ease_in(0)=0, ease_in(1)=1, gentler-than-linear midpoint). Keep the multiplicative exp() zoom-about-center and the pan clamp untouched. (3) Optional inertia: on key release, decay the last velocity over ~150-250ms instead of zeroing zoom_started/pan_started immediately — bigger change, own subtask, only if the owner still wants more polish after (1)+(2). Note the scroll-wheel/trackpad steps (WHEEL_ZOOM_STEP, PIXEL_ZOOM_STEP, WHEEL_PAN_STEP, PINCH_GAIN) are a SEPARATE input path (AppCore::scroll, not apply_view_holds) — the owner's note is about held-key motion, so leave the gesture constants unless they ask. Prime directive: this is off the photo hot path (only runs while a pan/zoom key is held), so feel is free to change; still no per-frame heap alloc. Consider whether any of these should become settings (nav ramp/start/max are already configurable) vs hard-coded; default to constants unless the owner wants a knob.
tasks.testStrategy: Primarily owner feel-test on device (Windows first, then confirm macOS/Linux unchanged-for-the-better): hold each pan direction and zoom in/out, confirm the start is gentle enough for fine framing and the top speed is comfortable, not lurchy. If the ramp is refactored into a pure ease helper, unit-test the curve (endpoints, monotonicity, gentler-than-linear midpoint). Regression: apply_view_holds still returns changed=true only while keys are held (loop keeps polling) and pan stays clamped to image bounds; keypress->photon nav timing is untouched (this path is nav-independent).

tasks.description: Owner ask (2026-07-09): let the mouse pointer hide, as an OPTION, on every platform where possible. Half the plumbing already exists but nothing actually hides today: contract::CursorKind::Hidden is defined (crates/pb-app-core/src/contract.rs:80) and its doc even claims 'the viewer hides the cursor in the chrome-free hot path and restores it on movement' — but (1) NOTHING in the core emits SetCursor(Hidden) (hover_cursor at app_core_impl.rs:2678-2686 only emits Grab/Grabbing/Pointer/Default), (2) the winit shell STUBS it: cursor_icon maps Hidden -> CursorIcon::Default (crates/pb-app/src/main.rs:3361, with the note 'Hidden is unused on the SetCursor path'), so Windows/Linux never hide, and (3) only the macOS shell honors it (CoreModel.swift:1897 NSCursor.setHiddenUntilMouseMoves(true)) — and even that is dead code since the core never sends it. So this is: wire a core auto-hide POLICY, make the winit shell truly hide, confirm macOS, and expose it as a setting. 'Where possible': winit uses Window::set_cursor_visible(false) (works on Windows + X11; on Wayland cursor visibility is compositor-mediated and may be a soft no-op — accept graceful degradation there).
tasks.details: Design: (a) POLICY in core — after N seconds with no CursorMoved (and no panel/dialog/menu open, and pointer not over a clickable affordance), emit CoreEffect::SetCursor(CursorKind::Hidden); any real pointer movement restores the resolved cursor (Default/Grab/etc via the existing hover_cursor path). Drive the timeout off the existing tick-deadline machinery (next_deadline / self.now) — do NOT add a spin; the app already sleeps when idle, so schedule a wake at the hide deadline. A natural stronger default: in the borderless Fullscreen 'speed mode' (WindowMode::Fullscreen) hide sooner or immediately-on-idle, since that mode is the chrome-free hot path the contract doc references. (b) WINIT SHELL — replace the Hidden->Default stub: on SetCursor(Hidden) call window.set_cursor_visible(false); on any other kind restore visibility + set the icon. Track visibility so we don't thrash set_cursor_visible every event. Windows + X11 honor it; Wayland may ignore — that's the 'where possible' caveat, log/accept. (c) macOS — the core now actually emits Hidden; verify setHiddenUntilMouseMoves gives the desired feel, or switch to explicit NSCursor.hide()/unhide() (persistent hide with our own restore-on-move) if the until-mouse-moves auto-restore fights the policy. (d) SETTING — add a serde-default bool (e.g. settings.hide_cursor_when_idle, maybe an idle-seconds too) and surface a toggle in BOTH shells (egui Settings General/Appearance tab via a pb-ui toggle_with_label + the SwiftUI SettingsView), defaulting per owner (likely ON in fullscreen, or a simple global ON/OFF). Privacy #2: cursor state is ephemeral runtime state; the only persisted bit is the toggle in settings.toml — no viewing trace. Keep the policy pure/testable in pb-app-core (feed it 'now' + last-move time + mode + overlay state, assert it emits Hidden after the timeout and restores on move) so it isn't a shell-only behavior.
tasks.testStrategy: Pure: unit-test the idle policy in pb-app-core — given last-move time, now, window mode, and whether an overlay/affordance is active, assert it decides Hidden after the timeout and Restore on movement, and never hides while a dialog/menu/hover-affordance is up. Manual per platform: Windows (winit) — leave the pointer still over a photo, confirm it vanishes after the timeout and reappears on the first move; confirm it does NOT hide while hovering the Cancel-scan chip or with a panel/menu open; confirm it hides sooner/at-idle in fullscreen speed mode. macOS — same feel via the SwiftUI shell. Linux — X11 hides; note Wayland behavior. Settings: toggling the option OFF disables all hiding on every platform; the setting round-trips through settings.toml (and the SwiftUI FFI) and nothing else is persisted.

tasks.title: Resolve LGPL static-link compliance (libheif/libde265 + FFmpeg) before public/commercial release
tasks.description:
The Windows binary statically links libheif + libde265, both LGPL-3.0. LGPL requires that users can relink the application against a modified version of the library - a static link alone does not satisfy this. Flagged in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md during the task #76 license audit (dav1d itself is BSD-2 and fully handled by the notices file; Linux AppImage bundles shared .so files so it already complies). Not urgent while the app is private/free, but a MUST before any public or commercial release (Velopack commercial plan).

CROSS-REF (2026-07-14, task #100): if #100 lands, FFmpeg (LGPL-2.1, no --enable-gpl) joins libheif/libde265 under this same obligation. Solve the relink story ONCE for all three rather than for libheif alone — #100.6 is written to defer to whatever this task decides. Do not close #77 with a libheif-only remedy without checking #100's status first.

=== UPDATE 2026-07-14: #100 HAS LANDED. This is no longer conditional. ===
Windows now statically links THREE LGPL libraries, not two: libheif 1.23.0 + libde265 1.1.1 (LGPL-3.0-or-later, §4) and FFmpeg 8.1.2 (LGPL-2.1-or-later, §6 — vcpkg's own copyright file confirms LGPL-2.1; gpl/nonfree features are opt-in and off). FFmpeg's role on Windows is narrow (demux/metadata only; MF still does 100% of decode) but that is IRRELEVANT to the obligation — LGPL attaches to distribution and linkage, not to how much of the library is called. dav1d stays fine (BSD-2-Clause, attribution only, already handled).

A SHIPPED-DOC DEFECT was found and fixed while reviewing this (2026-07-14). THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is copied into the Velopack package by release-windows.ps1:158 — i.e. it ships next to the exe as the user-facing legal notice — and it stated "**Windows does not use FFmpeg** (Media Foundation handles video there)". .taskmaster/docs/ffmpeg-compliance.md said the same, and its entire argument rested on it. Both were true when written and were made false by #100. A Windows build cut in that window would have distributed FFmpeg under notices affirmatively denying it — materially worse than a documented open item. Both docs + CLAUDE.md's Licensing section now state the Windows static link and flag it. The underlying obligation is unchanged; only the honesty of the paperwork was restored.

THE DECISION (owner): DLL linkage vs static + published relink materials.
* DLL (LGPL-2.1 §6(b) / LGPL-3.0 §4(d)(1)) — the conventional answer, already what macOS and Linux do, so it makes all three platforms tell one story. Cost: vcpkg dynamic triplet (x64-windows / arm64-windows) instead of *-windows-static-md; ffmpeg-sys-next then wants VCPKGRS_DYNAMIC=1 (the exact knob the `static` feature was added to defeat — see #100.1); build.rs changes; ~7 DLLs to stage, sign (Azure Trusted Signing) and ship per arch. NOT YET MEASURED: install size almost certainly grows — the +3.06 MB static figure exists because the linker discards every unreferenced object, and a DLL exports everything. That measurement should precede the call.
* Static + relink materials (LGPL-2.1 §6(a) / LGPL-3.0 §4(d)(0)) — legally recognized, and it keeps the small binary, but it requires publishing PhotoBlaze's OWN object files per release so a user can relink against a modified library. Object code, not source, so the proprietary position survives — but it is per-release, toolchain-specific plumbing that most vendors avoid for exactly that reason.
RECOMMENDATION: DLL. Measure the size delta first so the call is made on numbers.

=== MEASURED 2026-07-14 — the size objection to DLLs is DEAD (+0.8 MB). ===
Built the whole native stack against vcpkg's DYNAMIC x64-windows triplet (libheif[core], dav1d, ffmpeg with the SAME demux-only portfile trim) and compared like for like:
  STATIC  (ships today): exe 35.07 MB                       = 35.07 MB
  DYNAMIC (LGPL remedy): exe 29.04 MB + 7 DLLs 6.82 MB      = 35.87 MB
  DELTA: +0.80 MB (+2.3%) on-disk payload.
The going-in fear was a 10-15 MB regression, reasoning that a DLL exports everything while a static link lets the linker discard unreferenced objects. That reasoning was WRONG at this scale: the exe shrank 6.03 MB and the DLLs only weigh 6.82 MB back. Do not re-litigate this from intuition.

The DLLs (transitive closure of the real import table via dumpbin, not a guess): avcodec-62 1.94, dav1d 1.70, heif 1.33, avutil 0.84, avformat 0.54, libde265 0.35, swresample-6 0.12. NOTE swscale-9.dll is NOT needed — Windows only reads containers, so the scaler is never imported. VERIFIED RUNNING: photoblaze.exe copied to an empty dir with exactly those 7 DLLs starts and reports its version, so the set is complete (nothing is dlopen'd behind dumpbin's back — libheif's plugin loader is already OFF via the portfile patch).

HOW IT WAS BUILT (the seam is committed and inert by default):
* pb-decode/build.rs takes PB_VCPKG_DYNAMIC=1 -> the plain x64-windows / arm64-windows triplet and dylib= link kinds. Unset = today's static behaviour, byte for byte.
* FFmpeg additionally needs VCPKGRS_DYNAMIC=1 in the env. It does NOT need the ffmpeg-next 'static' feature removed: ffmpeg-sys-next only SETS that var when 'static' is off (build.rs:700-706) and never unsets it, so an externally-set value survives and the vcpkg crate honours it. That is why the whole spike flips on two env vars with no Cargo.toml edit — worth knowing, since #100.1 added 'static' specifically to defeat that variable.

STILL TO DO for a real DLL ship (none of it measured yet): setup-libheif.ps1 installs the dynamic triplet; release-windows.ps1 stages the 7 DLLs into $Stage and signs them (Azure Trusted Signing) alongside the exe; CI lanes; arm64. dav1d is BSD-2 so it could stay static, but one triplet supplies the tree — splitting it buys ~1.7 MB of DLL for extra build complexity, probably not worth it.

=== IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-14: Windows now links the LGPL libraries as DLLs by default. ===
The three obligations turned out to be INDEPENDENT, and all three are now addressed:
  1. LINKAGE (LGPL-2.1 6(b) / LGPL-3.0 4(d)(1)) - the default flipped to DLLs. build.rs
     `vcpkg_dynamic()` is now dynamic-by-default with `PB_VCPKG_STATIC=1` as the A/B escape
     hatch (the spike's polarity was the reverse: PB_VCPKG_DYNAMIC=1 opted IN). A
     PB_VCPKG_STATIC=1 build is the non-compliant configuration by definition and must never ship.
  2. LICENSE TEXT (LGPL-2.1 6 / LGPL-3.0 4(b)) - `licenses/` ships verbatim COPYING files for
     libheif, libde265, FFmpeg (LGPLv2.1) and dav1d, staged into the Velopack package, the macOS
     .app (Contents/Resources/licenses) and the AppImage (usr/share/licenses). This was MISSING ON
     EVERY PLATFORM and was the most exposed item: unlike the static link (which had 6(a) as a
     fallback defence), shipping without the licence text has no defence at all.
  3. ATTRIBUTION (LGPL-3.0 4(c)) - triggered only because About displays a copyright line; the
     About card now names each bundled library + its copyright and points at the licences folder.

FFmpeg follows the switch WITHOUT an env var: pb-decode's `ffmpeg-next` dep no longer enables the
`static` feature, and ffmpeg-sys-next sets VCPKGRS_DYNAMIC=1 itself exactly when `static` is absent.
Re-adding `features = ["static"]` there silently returns FFmpeg to a non-compliant static link -
Cargo.toml carries a warning comment saying so.

TWO TRAPS FOUND WHILE WIRING IT (both cost real time, both now handled + documented):
* libde265's import lib is `de265.lib` but its static lib is `libde265.lib` - the vcpkg triplets
  disagree on that ONE name (heif.lib and dav1d.lib are stable across both, and the DLL is still
  libde265.dll). A `dylib=libde265` link name gives LNK1181. The link name must track the triplet,
  not just the link kind.
* `Enter-VsDevShell` OVERWRITES VCPKG_ROOT with the vcpkg bundled inside Visual Studio - a tree with
  none of our pinned ports - even when the caller exported the right value first. Since ffprobe
  needs a Developer shell (bindgen), EVERY shipped build passes through this. scripts/vs-dev-env.ps1
  now captures VCPKG_ROOT and restores it (falling back to ~/vcpkg like build.rs does, because
  ffmpeg-sys-next has no such fallback and would otherwise hunt for FFmpeg in the VS tree).

Also: build.rs copies the vcpkg DLLs into target/<profile>/ AND target/<profile>/deps/ (Windows
resolves from the executable's own directory, and cargo puts tests in deps/), so `cargo run`/`cargo
test` work with no PATH dance and the shipped DLL set is the one the tests ran against.

REMAINING before this can be closed:
* ARM64 is UNVERIFIED end to end (no ARM64 box) - the dynamic triplet, the de265.lib naming and the
  DLL staging are all x64-measured only.
* No release has actually been cut with the DLL config yet; release-windows.ps1 stages the DLLs via a
  dumpbin transitive import walk and signs them, but that path is untested against a real `vpk pack`.
* The `cargo license` sweep of the rest of the dependency tree (per this task's details) is still not
  done.
tasks.details:
Options, roughly in order of practicality: (1) Ship libheif+libde265 as DLLs inside the Velopack package - Velopack handles loose DLLs next to the exe; LGPL is then satisfied by user-replaceability; needs a vcpkg dynamic triplet build (x64-windows + arm64-windows, dynamic CRT implications to check) and a build.rs link switch. (2) Offer relink materials (publish the app's object files or a static archive on request) - legally valid, operationally clunky. (3) Replace libheif/libde265 with a non-LGPL path (WIC-only HEIC would lose the measured ~4.9x parallel decode win; a BSD HEVC decoder does not realistically exist). (4) Counsel review if commercial licensing of libheif (strukturag offers commercial terms) turns out cheaper than the engineering. Also do a quick sweep of the rest of the dependency tree (cargo license) for any other copyleft surprises while at it.

=== VALIDATED 2026-07-14 (x64) — the DLL ship path is no longer untested. ===
The 0.2.1 x64 release was cut and PUBLISHED with the DLL config, which closes the second of the three
REMAINING items above ("No release has actually been cut with the DLL config yet ... untested against a
real vpk pack"). Evidence, from the shipped BlazeViewer-0.2.1-full.nupkg:
* The dumpbin transitive import walk staged exactly the 7 DLLs this task measured — avcodec-62,
  avformat-62, avutil-60, dav1d, heif, libde265, swresample-6 — and swscale-9 was correctly ABSENT
  (Windows only reads containers, so the scaler is never imported). The computed set matched the
  measurement with no hand-editing.
* All 7 DLLs + blazeviewer.exe + the ExecutionStub + Squirrel.exe are Authenticode Valid, signed
  FullSpec Systems (Azure Trusted Signing). vpk signs the pack dir contents by default, as assumed.
* licenses/ (libheif, libde265, ffmpeg LGPLv2.1, dav1d COPYING) + THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md ship inside
  the package payload alongside the exe — obligations 2 and 3 verified in the artifact, not just in
  the script.
* The packaged exe, run from the extracted payload with only those 7 DLLs beside it, starts and
  reports "Blaze Viewer 0.2.1 (dc9dc48)" — so the closure is complete and nothing is dlopen d behind
  dumpbin s back, now confirmed on a real signed package rather than a hand-assembled dir.
STILL OPEN (unchanged): ARM64 end-to-end (no ARM64 box), and the cargo license sweep of the rest of
the dependency tree. Keep this task in-progress until those land.

tasks.title: CLI polish: clap, --help/--version, session-override flags, Windows console attach
tasks.description: Make PhotoBlaze a pleasant cross-platform CLI citizen for scripted launches. Today (main.rs:3406-3525): hand-rolled args, no --help/--version, unknown flags silently swallowed; release Windows builds are GUI-subsystem so nothing can print anyway. Decision (owner, 2026-07-11): use clap 4 (derive) - binary cost is a rounding error on this exe, parse time is launch-only, and it buys polished help/typo suggestions/value validation/completions for a low-usage feature. clap lives in pb-app ONLY (pb-app-core stays toml-only per NS0); the CLI parses into a plain LaunchOverrides struct the core consumes. Overrides NEVER persist to settings.toml (a scripted --dark --slideshow=5 launch must not rewrite the user's config).
tasks.details:
Order of operations in main(): (1) Velopack --veloapp-* intercept stays FIRST (update.rs:402); (2) Windows: AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS) + rebind stdout/stderr BEFORE parsing (clap's help/errors are invisible without it; known cosmetic PowerShell prompt-interleave wart is acceptable); (3) clap parse; (4) launch. Register the hidden dev flags (--hud-gallery, --egui-shot, --settings-shot, --light, --tab, --welcome, --metrics) as hide=true so clap doesn't error on them. Parse-error fallback: no console attached (double-click / file association) -> existing Message dialog instead of a silent exit; console -> normal stderr + exit 2. Flag set (long + short where sensible), all mapping to existing state per the 2026-07-11 survey: --fullscreen/-f, --windowed/-w (exist); --recursive/-r, --no-recursive (exist); --info/--no-info (settings.show_image_info); --details (Panels.inspector, the Shift+I inspector); --folders (folder_tree_open); --slideshow[=SECS] (slideshow + interval); --scale <fit|fill|original> (scale_mode); --theme <light|dark|system> (appearance_mode); --mute (mute_live_audio); --shuffle (NEW small feature: start nav in the precomputed pb-core shuffle order - randomness today is per-keypress, not a mode); --version (build.rs build-id stamp, same string as About). Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage/bad path (with stderr message when console attached). Docs: README CLI section; optional clap_complete completions later. Estimate: 1-2 focused days; the AttachConsole shim is the only fiddly part.

RESOLVED DECISIONS (owner Q&A, 2026-07-11, branch feat/cli-clap): (a) STRICTNESS = Mixed - clamp an out-of-range --slideshow=SECS into [0.1s,60s] (matches the runtime slider's own clamp); --fullscreen + --windowed together = last-one-wins (no clap conflict error); a NONEXISTENT positional path still errors (exit 2, stderr when console). Unknown flags / bad enum values keep clap's own exit 2. (b) EXTRAS beyond #78's set: ADD --start-at <N|name> (open at the Nth photo, 1-based, or a matching filename, instead of the first; wins over --shuffle's random start; filename match applied once the deferred scan resolves). RESERVE --new-window as a parse-accepted no-op now, so the future single-instance task #1 has its documented bypass seam and clap won't reject it later. --sort <name|date|size|random> is DEFERRED (owner: cool idea but do it as a coherent app-wide sort-order feature first, not a CLI-only bolt-on); do NOT parse-accept it yet. (c) --shuffle MECHANICS (trivial - reuses existing last_nav-steers-slideshow design, app_core_impl.rs:2550-2553 + 1054): set last_nav = Nav::Random at launch so the slideshow AND hold-to-blaze auto-advance in the precomputed random order; a DIRECTORY launch also does one random jump when the playlist resolves (start on a random photo); a SPECIFIC-FILE launch honors that file as the start (no random jump) but still sets last_nav=Random for a later slideshow. Manual Next/Prev (space/backspace) stay SEQUENTIAL and steer the slideshow back to sequential - the existing contract, matching the owner's ask (random slideshow advance + random dir-start, not random manual stepping). Flip to full mode later if wanted. (d) TDD: Cli->LaunchOverrides is a pure mapping unit-tested via Cli::try_parse_from([...]); --shuffle/--reverse/--start-at get pb-core/app-core tests. LaunchOverrides is a plain Option-field struct in pb-app-core (no clap dep); AppCore applies it, never persists. Docs: README CLI section + CHANGELOG (Added). Note: task ids were stringified by the adding commit; normalized #78 back to numeric per the tasks.json convention. (e) --reverse ADDED (owner, 2026-07-11): a direction seam over the four existing Nav variants, all routed through the launch last_nav (the slideshow + hold-to-blaze already advance via last_nav, app_core_impl.rs:1054, and toggle_slideshow does NOT reset it :5102). Mapping: neither flag=Forward, --reverse=Backward, --shuffle=Random, --shuffle+--reverse=RandomPrev (reverse shuffle - already the Shift+Enter/RandomPrev action, keymap.rs:499). Directory start position: --shuffle=random photo, --reverse=LAST photo (runway to play backward), default=first; a specific-file launch always honors the file; --start-at wins over both. Runtime discoverability stays CLI-only here - the 'tap Left/Backspace during a running slideshow to reverse' steer already works emergently (manual nav steers the slideshow) and will just be documented; a dedicated runtime reverse toggle/menu item is a possible future micro-task. (f) ARCHITECTURE REVISION (owner, 2026-07-11): macOS CLI parity is now wanted 'now-ish' (owner finishes/tests on a real Mac later), so the clap parser is extracted into a NEW shared LIB crate `pb-cli` (depends on pb-app-core + clap) instead of living inside the pb-app BINARY - a binary crate can't be a dependency, and pb-app-core must stay clap-free (NS0). pb-app depends on pb-cli; later pb-mac-ffi depends on pb-cli too and exposes one FFI entry that feeds Swift's CommandLine.arguments through the SAME parser. pb-cli is FFI-ready by design: parse_from(args-iterator) -> Result<Cli, clap::Error> with NO process::exit (help/version/errors are clap::Error kinds each shell renders itself - which also serves the Windows AttachConsole + no-console Message-dialog fallback), and argv is always a parameter (never std::env inside the lib). The render-and-exit dev commands (--hud-gallery/--egui-shot/--settings-shot + --light/--tab/--welcome) STAY intercepted in pb-app before clap (as today), so the shared Cli holds only the real cross-platform flags (+ hidden --metrics). subtasks.title: Decode text cues to timed plain text
subtasks.description: DONE 2026-07-15. BOTH tiers ship. Sidecars: SubRip + WebVTT parsed in pure Rust (cues.rs). EMBEDDED streams: pb_decode::ffmpeg::cues (ff_stream_subtitle_cues) demuxes + avcodec_decode_subtitle2 for MKV subrip/ass/webvtt and MP4 mov_text. Lives at the `ffprobe` level, NOT beside demux.rs (which is ffvideo-gated = absent on Windows): reading a subtitle stream needs a demuxer + a SUBTITLE decoder, never a video one, so the trimmed Windows FFmpeg serves it — resolving the #100.8 constraint (sidecars stay pure-Rust and never touch FFmpeg, so Windows' missing srt/webvtt/ass DEMUXER is moot; no need to widen the trim). KEY FACT: FFmpeg normalizes EVERY text decoder's output to one ASS envelope (ff_ass_get_dialog: 8 commas then Text), so text_cue::ass_event_text (pure, tested) is the only wire-format knowledge needed. STREAMING (the design that makes it usable): reading cues is a full linear pass over the container — MEASURED 39 s on the corpus MKV (4.4 GB over SMB) — because subtitle blocks are scattered through every cluster. As a blocking wait that is indistinguishable from broken. But the reader walks in presentation order at ~70x the rate playback consumes, so it hands cues over as it finds them: MEASURED first batch at 1.06 s, 177 batches, cancellation stops a read in ~1 s not 40. CueLoad::drop cancels, so a nav can't leave a worker chewing 20 GB. FUTURE OPT: the playback demuxer already reads these packets and discards them — forwarding them would make cues cost zero I/O, but it only exists on routes using OUR demuxer, and a feature must never be gated on a backend. Layer it under, never replace. TWO ffmpeg-next LANDMINES FOUND: (1) NO Drop for Subtitle and it never calls avsubtitle_free — leaks per cue unless you free it yourself; (2) Text::get/Ass::get are from_utf8_unchecked = UB on the non-UTF-8 payloads that really exist (CP1252 .srt muxed without sub_charenc). We read the C string lossily via raw ptr instead. MOJIBAKE REPAIR (pb_app_core::mojibake, 15 tests): the corpus MKV carries `â™ª` where `♪` belongs — VERIFIED with `ffprobe -show_data` to be IN THE FILE, not our bug. Undone only when provable: re-encode a run to CP1252, require the bytes be valid UTF-8. `café` fails that (E9 is a lead with no continuation) so it is untouched. Applied per-RUN, not whole-string, at the single choke point (CueTrack::from_cues) BOTH tiers pass through. ⚠ SAFE_LEADS excludes à/á on purpose: French 'voilà «' (E0 A0 AB) IS valid UTF-8 and a naive round-trip corrupts it into a Samaritan letter — pinned by a test. Cost: mojibake'd Thai/Devanagari stays broken; the right trade. Also needed the 5 WHATWG windows-1252 passthrough bytes (0x81/8D/8F/90/9D) — `”` is E2 80 9D, so without 0x9D every CLOSING curly quote stays broken while the opening one repairs. Found by a test, not the spec.

tasks.title: Playback bar: subtitle toggle (C) + audio/subtitle cycling (A) + track picker popover
tasks.description: [2026-07-15: the Shift+C cycle slice is DONE — Action::SubtitleCycle + keymap + AppCore::cycle_subtitle_track + toast via #98's track_summary, with cycle_choices/next_choice pure and unit-tested in subtitle.rs. Off is a real first row; Automatic is not a step but the cycle advances PAST what it resolves to. REMAINING: the A/Shift+A audio cycling, the CC button + popover, and the egui/native presenters.] Add the SELECTION affordances for subtitles and audio tracks to the video playback bar — the action half of the pair whose description half is task #98. Two controls: (1) a closed-captioning icon button, shown only when the clip has at least one subtitle track, that toggles subtitles on/off with a single click, bound to C on the keyboard (Shift+C cycles subtitle tracks; A / Shift+A cycle audio tracks, each toasting the result); (2) a settings icon that opens a small popover holding two lists — audio track and subtitle track — for picking among them. Deliberately NOT an Inspector tab and NOT a modal dialog. Not a tab because the Inspector's contract (overlay.rs:28) is "three facets of tell me about this image" — read-only description — and track selection is a write that changes what the app is doing right now; a control does not belong in a description panel, and two video-only tabs would also make the tab bar change shape between a JPEG and an MKV. Not a modal because choosing a track is an A/B comparison — you pick a track to hear or read whether it is the right one — and a modal blocks the very feedback loop the choice depends on. Every player that feels good at this (IINA, Infuse, VLC, QuickTime, YouTube) uses a transient popover over live playback.
tasks.details:
SUPERSEDES the "Track selection UI/keybinding (cycle subtitle track / off)" clause of task #90 subtask 1 — that subtask keeps stream/sidecar DISCOVERY and hands the UI here, so the two tasks do not both grow a picker.

Home: the existing hover-reveal controls zone / playback line (AppCore::flash_video_controls, app_core_impl.rs:7388). Both controls live there, appear with the bar, and fade with it. Reuse the reveal + re-arm timing already built; interacting with either control must re-arm the reveal so the bar does not fade out from under an open popover.

Icons: the icon system is semantic Font Awesome (pb-ui/src/icon.rs — add an Icon variant and vendor icons/<family>/<name>.svg for EVERY family, per that module's contract). For the subtitle toggle, FA's `closed-captioning` (solid + regular both exist) is the answer to "not sure what that looks like" — it is the near-universal glyph, matching SF `captions.bubble`. Suggested variant name Icon::Captions. For the picker, Icon::Sliders ALREADY EXISTS (SF `slider.horizontal.3`, used by Settings ▸ General) — prefer reusing it over vendoring a new gear, unless the Settings association is confusing in a playback context, in which case FA `gear` as Icon::Gear.

States: the captions button needs three, not two — no subtitle tracks (button absent entirely, do not show a dead control), subtitles off (dimmed/outline), subtitles on (accent-tinted, matching the app's accent-color source per task #85). Hiding rather than disabling is the right call: a photo viewer's playback bar should not carry a permanently dead CC button for the 95% of clips that are phone videos with no subs.

Keybinding: C = toggle subtitles on/off; Shift+C = cycle to the next subtitle track, toasting its name. Mnemonic: Captions — it matches the closed-captioning glyph the button wears, and it reads to someone who has never opened a terminal. VERIFIED FREE (2026-07-14): the bare single-letter bindings are Y D I M O P R T S, and the only C chords in keymap.rs are Cmd+C (Copy), Ctrl+C, Shift+Cmd+C, Shift+Ctrl+C — bare C and Shift+C are both unclaimed. Owner sign-off 2026-07-14.

DO NOT use J. An earlier draft of this task proposed it, justified as "mpv's subtitle key, so the muscle memory already exists." That justification was wrong twice over; it is recorded here so nobody re-derives it. Wrong on the facts: mpv's actual etc/input.conf reads `j cycle sub` (switch TRACK), `J cycle sub down` (switch track BACKWARDS), `v cycle sub-visibility` (the real toggle), `# cycle audio`. So J-as-toggle hands the wrong verb to the exact fingers it claimed to borrow from, and a Shift+J cycle-forward would have collided with mpv's cycle-BACKWARD — same chord, reverse direction, which is worse than an arbitrary key because arbitrary keys fight nobody. Wrong on the reasoning: mpv's audience is a thin sliver of CLI users who hand-edit input.conf, while PhotoBlaze's audience double-clicks a JPEG — a convention imported from a near-disjoint user base buys nothing. And there is no cross-player consensus to defer to anyway: VLC's `v` cycles the subtitle TRACK while mpv's `v` toggles VISIBILITY — same key, opposite verbs, in the two most-used players. Mnemonic beats lineage.

Add all four via the normal keymap path — one(Action::SubtitleToggle, "C"), one(Action::SubtitleCycle, "Shift+C"), one(Action::AudioCycle, "A"), one(Action::AudioCyclePrev, "Shift+A") — so every one surfaces in the Help panel and stays remappable in Settings ▸ Shortcuts. Never hardcode a chord.

Audio: A = cycle to the next audio track; Shift+A = cycle to the previous. Each toasts the newly-selected track's summary. VERIFIED FREE (2026-07-14): no A chord of any kind is bound in keymap.rs — not bare, not Cmd, not Ctrl, not Shift. Owner sign-off 2026-07-14, overriding this task's earlier draft which withheld a bare key from audio until switching was proven solid; the owner's call is that the affordance earns its keys now.

Shift-verb asymmetry — DELIBERATE, do not silently "fix" it: Shift+C cycles subtitle tracks FORWARD (bare C is spent on the on/off toggle), while Shift+A cycles audio BACKWARD (bare A is already the forward cycle). So Shift reads as "cycle" on C and "reverse" on A. This is not an oversight. It falls out of the shape of the two features: subtitles have two verbs (toggle + pick) because they have an Off state, audio has one (pick) because it never does. Any scheme that makes Shift mean one thing across both keys has to spend a third key or drop the subtitle toggle, which are both worse trades. Escape hatch if it grates in real use: drop Shift+A entirely — with the 1-2 audio tracks most files carry, forward and backward cycling are the same keypress, and Shift+A stays free for later.

TOAST ON CONFIRMED SWITCH, NOT ON KEYPRESS — this is the one that will bite. Audio switching is the risky path (the master-clock re-prime noted below), so the toast must fire when the new track is actually producing sound, and must report failure if the switch stalls. A toast reading "Track 2 · English · Commentary" over silently-dead audio is worse than no toast at all: it tells the user the app is fine at the exact moment it is not, and it trains them to distrust every other toast in the app. Subtitle switching is cheap and may toast optimistically; audio may not. If the switch cannot be confirmed within a short window, toast the failure and stay on the old track.

Reserved elsewhere — do not spend: bare E is informally earmarked for Export (task #89, the image conversion/export mode), per owner 2026-07-14. Not locked, but do not claim it here.

Build the Shift+C cycle+toast slice FIRST (Toast/ToastIcon already exist in overlay.rs). It is cheap, needs no new UI construct, and covers most real use — usually the user is not choosing from a list, they are going "no, not that one, next." It will tell you whether the popover is urgent before you build it.

The popover: yes, it is fundamentally two lists — but the wrinkles that make it more than two lists are the actual work, and skipping them is what makes players feel broken:
  - Subtitles need an explicit "Off" ROW at the top of the list. Off is a real selectable item, not the absence of a selection. Audio has no Off (there is always exactly one active track, unless the clip is silent, in which case the audio list is absent).
  - Both lists are single-select radio semantics, not checkboxes, and need a visible checkmark on the active row.
  - Rows reuse the same summary strings task #98 builds (language · codec · layout · disposition) — build that formatter ONCE in pb-app-core and let both the Details panel and this popover consume it. Do not format tracks twice.
  - Sidecar .srt/.vtt entries (task #90.1) appear in the subtitle list alongside embedded tracks.
  - Forced-subtitle tracks are worth surfacing as such — users looking for the foreign-dialogue-only track will otherwise pick the full SDH track and be annoyed.
  - Selection must apply WITHOUT pausing, seeking, or restarting playback, and the popover must not steal focus in a way that eats the space/arrow transport keys while open. Audio track switching mid-playback is the risky one: it needs to re-prime the audio session against the master clock (see the reprime-after-device-change work in task #91) rather than tear down and rebuild.
  - Dismiss on click-outside, Escape, and on picking a row.

Shell parity: this needs a presenter in BOTH shells (egui in pb-app, native in pb-mac-ffi) with a shell-neutral model in pb-app-core — same split as panels.rs/panels_ui.rs. The model (track lists, active indices, open/closed) belongs in core and should be unit-testable with no egui/AppKit. On macOS the native presentation is an NSMenu or a popover off the button; on Windows/egui it is an egui popup anchored to the button rect.

Do not over-build. Two lists, a checkmark, an Off row. No search, no per-track delay/sync offset UI (a real feature in mpv/IINA, but out of scope here — log it if wanted), no styling controls (those are task #90 subtask 4's Settings, correctly placed there, not duplicated in the popover).
tasks.testStrategy:
Pure: unit-test the shell-neutral popover model in pb-app-core — track list construction from a probe result (Off row present and first for subtitles, absent for audio; active index reflected; sidecars included; forced marked), selection transitions, and open/close state. Assert the track summary formatter is the SAME code path the Details panel (task #98) uses, so the two can never drift. Assert the keymap resolves C -> SubtitleToggle, Shift+C -> SubtitleCycle, A -> AudioCycle, Shift+A -> AudioCyclePrev; that all four appear in the Help panel model (not hardcoded); and that none shadows Cmd+C (Copy) — bare and modified chords must stay distinct, the property keymap.rs already asserts for S vs Cmd+S. Unit-test cycle wrap-around in both directions, and that cycling a single-track clip is a no-op that does not toast.

Manual, on the Captain Phillips MKV and a multi-audio-track MP4: hover to reveal the bar; confirm the CC button appears only when subtitle tracks exist and is absent (not dead) on a phone clip; C toggles subs on/off and the button state tracks it; Shift+C cycles and toasts the track name; A / Shift+A cycle audio forward/back and toast; Cmd+C still copies; open the picker, switch subtitle track and confirm the change lands within a cue or two without a pause; switch AUDIO track mid-playback and confirm no stall, no desync, no dropout — the master clock holds (the failure mode task #91 chased). Confirm the bar does not fade while the popover is open, Escape and click-outside dismiss it, and space/arrows still drive the transport with the popover closed. Verify on both shells (egui + macOS native) and confirm Settings ▸ Shortcuts can remap C and Shift+C. Audio-toast honesty check (the failure this task most cares about): force an audio switch to stall or fail (unplug the output device mid-switch, or a deliberately broken track) and confirm the toast reports the FAILURE rather than cheerfully naming a track that is not playing — and that playback falls back to the previous track rather than dying silent.

tasks.title: Windows: FFmpeg demux/metadata backend (subtitle tracks; unblocks #90/#99)
tasks.description:
Enable FFmpeg on the Windows build for CONTAINER PARSING ONLY — the track catalog now, subtitle cues for #90 later. Media Foundation keeps poster + playback (hardware decode, low latency, 79.10 GPU decode): this is explicitly NOT a decode change. It mirrors the split macOS already runs (AVFoundation + ffvideo fallback).

WHY NOW (98.5 spike, 2026-07-14): every previous rejection of FFmpeg-on-Windows rested on the premise "MF can do it" — the WASAPI audio fix proved that premise right for audio. It is now provably FALSE for subtitles. MF media sources do not model subtitle tracks at all: the presentation descriptor (the source's own complete stream table, not something the reader filters) reports 3 streams for a multitrack.mkv holding 1 video + 2 audio + 4 SUBTITLE tracks, and 3 for a multitrack.mp4 with 2 tx3g tracks. No reader flag adds a descriptor to a source's PD, and nothing hides under another major type. There is no MF-native fix to prefer this time, so the argument that kept FFmpeg out does not reach this case.

CONSEQUENCE: #90 (subtitle rendering) and #99 (subtitle picker) have NO Windows path today. #90 already specifies subtitles are "decoded through the existing FFmpeg backend (task #84)" — satisfied on Linux/macOS, never reconciled with Windows. MF cannot supply cue samples any more than the track list.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED:
1. The Rust side is ALREADY platform-neutral: ffmpeg/ is gated #[cfg(feature = "ffmpeg")] with no unix/not(windows) gate. `cargo check -p pb-decode --features ffvideo` on Windows gave ZERO Rust errors — it reached ffmpeg-sys-next's build.rs and died on pkg-config not finding libavutil. Purely a build-system problem.
2. ffmpeg-sys-next 8.1 build.rs tries FFMPEG_DIR (:1033), then vcpkg::find_package("ffmpeg") (:696/701, msvc-only), and only then pkg-config (:1088 — the panic we saw). So the integration path is the one setup-libheif.ps1 ALREADY uses: install the ffmpeg port into the pinned vcpkg tree and the crate finds it automatically. NO pkg-config needed.
3. ffmpeg/tracks.rs is the REFERENCE backend and is fully tested. Windows goes from the weakest backend to parity on code already written — and gains the dispositions + named channel layout MF hides (the honest-degradation list in mf_tracks.rs).
4. Licensing is ALREADY owed: #77 exists because Windows statically links libheif + libde265 (LGPL-3.0) with an unresolved relink obligation that is a MUST before commercial release. FFmpeg is LGPL-2.1 without --enable-gpl (vcpkg's ffmpeg is LGPL by default; gpl is opt-in). Same remedy — one fix covers both; marginal cost is a notices entry.

SIZE — MEASURED AND SETTLED. Final figure, re-measured 2026-07-14 from the COMMITTED recipe on the real pinned tree (the earlier +3.44 MB came from the spike's scratch overlay and is superseded): the trimmed build costs **+3.06 MB** (31.98 -> 35.04 MB release exe, +9.6%), with all 8 ffmpeg/tracks.rs tests passing. The untrimmed ffmpeg[core] cost +16.42 MB (+51.3%); the difference is entirely video decoders we never call, since MF does all decode. At 3 MB the size objection is closed and a download-on-demand scheme is NOT worth its complexity (Velopack's versioned app dir, DLL signing, offline first-run, and a content-triggered network fetch sitting badly with privacy #2).

COST (honest): a build/release-pipeline project, not an afternoon — vcpkg FFmpeg for x64 AND arm64 (each on its native box; no cross toolchain is wired up), a setup-script change, installer weight, and pulling #77 forward.

ALTERNATIVE IF THIS IS REFUSED: a hand-rolled EBML/Matroska metadata parser (~400 lines + its own fuzz target, avis.rs precedent) gets MKV subtitle tracks + dispositions with zero build/licensing/size impact — but covers MKV only, does not advance #90's cues, and is throwaway if #90 lands on FFmpeg as designed.

=== STATUS 2026-07-14: the FEATURE IS LANDED AND SHIPPING-READY on x64. Subtasks 1-5 + 7 are done; 6 and 8 are deliberately out of scope for this pass (owner: "everything except LGPL"). ===
Windows Details now reads a container exactly the way Linux/macOS do, via the same reference backend. Two things remain BEFORE a release actually goes out, and they are the reason this task is not `done`:
* **6 (LGPL) is a genuine BLOCKER for a commercial release, not paperwork.** FFmpeg is statically linked (-static-md), which does not by itself satisfy LGPL-2.1's relink requirement — the identical unresolved question as #77 (libheif/libde265, LGPL-3.0). It needs the owner's static-vs-dynamic call, and one decision covers both. Shipping the current build to the public without settling this is exactly the exposure #77 already flags as a MUST.
* **8 (#90/#99 reconcile)**: the subtitle *decoders* are already in the trimmed build (subrip/ass/movtext/webvtt), so the Windows cue path is unblocked — but #90/#99 still describe a backend Windows did not have, and should be re-read now that it does.
* ARM64 is wired (setup script + CI lane) but UNVERIFIED — no ARM64 box was available. See 100.7.

subtasks.title: Spike: link FFmpeg here and prove real Windows subtitle output
subtasks.description:
Lowest-regret first step, BEFORE any release-pipeline work. Install the ffmpeg port into the pinned vcpkg tree (same -VcpkgRef commit as libheif/dav1d) and confirm vcpkg::find_package("ffmpeg") resolves with no pkg-config. Then run ff_probe_video_details over tests/fixtures/video/multitrack.mkv and confirm Windows reports the 4 subtitle tracks + 2 audio WITH dispositions — the existing ffmpeg/tracks.rs::multitrack_mkv_* tests should pass unchanged on Windows. Record the resulting lib/DLL size. DECISION GATE: if size or build pain is unacceptable, fall back to the EBML parser in the description and close this task.

MEASURED during 100.1: the ALREADY-pinned vcpkg tree (a0400024711b283056538ac19ced80b91a83c24c) carries ffmpeg 8.1.2, an exact match for ffmpeg-sys-next 8.1 — the pin does NOT need to move, which was the biggest going-in risk. The vcpkg crate's default triplets (x64-windows-static-md / arm64-windows-static-md) already match the project's pinned triplets on both arches, so no VCPKGRS_TRIPLET is needed. Windows DOES need ffmpeg-next's `static` feature: without it ffmpeg-sys-next sets VCPKGRS_DYNAMIC=1 and the vcpkg crate resolves the dynamic x64-windows triplet instead (wired as a [target."cfg(windows)".dependencies] entry so Linux/macOS keep linking system FFmpeg).

=== RESULT (2026-07-14): PROVEN. The gate is PASSED on capability; the size call is the owner's. ===
* vcpkg `ffmpeg[core,avcodec,avformat,swresample,swscale]:x64-windows-static-md` built from the ALREADY-pinned tree in 11 min. ffmpeg-sys-next resolved it via vcpkg with NO pkg-config (build.rs emitted cargo:ffmpeg_8_1=true).
* The existing crates/pb-decode/src/ffmpeg/tracks.rs tests PASS UNMODIFIED ON WINDOWS — all 8, including multitrack_mkv_subtitles_carry_flags_capability_and_non_latin_metadata and catalog_matches_the_ffprobe_oracle.
* Real Details output on Windows for multitrack.mkv (FFmpeg backend):
    Audio
    Track 1: English · AAC stereo · 44.1 kHz · Default
    Track 2: French · AC-3 5.1(side) · 48 kHz · Commentary
    Subtitles
    Track 1: English · SubRip · Default
    Track 2: English (SDH) · SubRip · Forced
    Track 3: Spanish · PGS · Unsupported
    Track 4: Japanese · SubRip · 日本語字幕
  All THREE honest degradations recorded in mf_tracks.rs vanish at once: subtitles listed, dispositions present, layouts named (stereo / 5.1(side) instead of "2 channels" / "6 channels"). multitrack.mp4's tx3g resolves as "Timed Text"; black_then_color.mp4 still correctly says Audio: No / Subtitles: No.
* SIZE (release photoblaze.exe): baseline --features libheif,dav1d = 31.98 MB; + ffvideo = 48.40 MB. DELTA = +16.42 MB (+51.3%). This is the UNTRIMMED ceiling: full ffvideo, every FFmpeg codec. avcodec's codec registry references every enabled codec so the linker cannot drop any — which is exactly what subtask 5 removes. Subtask 5 is now clearly worth doing, and its target should be re-measured against this 16.42 MB number.
* Landed to enable it (safe, inert without the feature): a [target."cfg(windows)".dependencies] ffmpeg-next entry adding ONLY `static`, and build.rs::link_ffmpeg_windows_syslibs. Default build verified unaffected: 468 + 218 tests pass, clippy -D warnings clean.
* BUILD-ENV requirements found (all needed by subtask 7 / CI): VCPKG_ROOT must be exported; LIBCLANG_PATH must point at libclang (bindgen) — VS 2022 already ships it at VC\Tools\Llvm\{x64,ARM64}\bin, so NO new install, and the ARM64 copy exists for the arm64 box; and the build MUST run inside a VS Developer shell (Enter-VsDevShell) because bindgen's clang needs INCLUDE for stdint.h — a plain cargo build does not need this, so it is a new constraint on the release script.
* ffmpeg-sys-next emits only ole32/secur32/ws2_32/bcrypt/user32; static FFmpeg 8.1 also needs crypt32 + ncrypt (avformat tls_schannel.o) and mfuuid + strmiids (avcodec mfenc.o/mf_utils.o — FFmpeg's own MF *encoder*, dead weight we only link to satisfy LNK2019; subtask 5 should remove the objects entirely).

subtasks.title: Cargo feature: metadata-only ffmpeg (no producer/poster)
subtasks.description:
`ffvideo` pulls the full cross-platform video backend (producer + poster) — Windows must NOT take that, MF owns playback. Add a narrower feature (e.g. `ffprobe`) pulling dep:ffmpeg-next + ffmpeg/{init,io,probe,color,tracks} and the ff_probe_video_details export, WITHOUT ffmpeg/{video_producer,poster}. Note ff_probe_video_details currently lives in ffmpeg/poster.rs (re-exported at lib.rs:147), so it likely needs moving or re-gating. Drop software-scaling/software-resampling from the ffmpeg-next feature list on this path — metadata needs neither.

=== RESULT (2026-07-14): DONE. ===
* New `ffprobe = ["ffmpeg"]` feature; `ffvideo = ["ffmpeg", "ffprobe"]` now implies it (ffvideo needs the same probes and adds decode on top). Pass-throughs added to pb-app-core + pb-app.
* As predicted, the probes had to move: new crates/pb-decode/src/ffmpeg/details.rs holds ff_probe_video_details / ff_probe_video_input / stream_info / decoder_for, split out of poster.rs so a build can read containers without linking the decode path. poster.rs keeps only ff_decode_video_poster.
* THE IMPORTANT ONE — a NEW fn was required, and only the wiring test (100.3) found it: ff_probe_video_details CANNOT be the Windows entry point. It calls stream_info -> decoder_for, which needs an H.264/HEVC *video decoder* — exactly what the trimmed build (100.5) removes. On a demuxers-only build it returns Err for every real video, so the wiring silently fell back to MF and the panel would have shipped saying "MediaFoundation" with no subtitles. Added `ff_probe_tracks` (catalog only, opens the container and reads the stream table, needs no decoder) and pointed Windows at that. This is the one place where 100.5's trim and 100.3's wiring interact, and it fails silently rather than loudly.
* NOT done as specced: software-scaling/software-resampling are still in the base ffmpeg-next feature list. Dropping them for ffprobe-only would need a second cfg'd dep entry, and they cost ~8 MB of .lib but only ~0 of the exe (the linker drops what the trimmed build never references — the +3.06 MB is measured WITH them present). Not worth the Cargo complexity; revisit if the exe delta ever moves.
* ffmpeg/mod.rs takes #![cfg_attr(not(feature = "ffvideo"), allow(dead_code))] — the shared helpers have members only the producer/poster use.

subtasks.title: Wire the Windows catalog to FFmpeg, keep MF for the video facts

subtasks.title: Minimal FFmpeg build: measure first, then trim
subtasks.description:
MF keeps ALL video/audio decode, so this build needs avformat/avcodec/avutil + demuxers (matroska, mov, avi, asf, mpegts) and — for #90 — the text subtitle decoders (subrip, ass, movtext, webvtt), and NO video/audio decoders. vcpkg's ffmpeg[core] is broad by default; a --disable-everything --enable-demuxer=... build likely needs an overlay port. MEASURE the default first (subtask 1): if it is acceptable, do not build a custom port for its own sake. MUST NOT enable vcpkg's `gpl` feature (x264 etc.) — that would make the binary GPL and is incompatible with the commercial plan.

=== RESULT (2026-07-14): DONE — recipe proven, +3.06 MB, all 8 tracks tests pass. ===
Overlay port patching ports/ffmpeg/portfile.cmake at the anchor
  set(OPTIONS "--enable-pic --disable-doc --enable-runtime-cpudetect --disable-autodetect")
with string(APPEND OPTIONS ...):
  --disable-everything --disable-network --disable-encoders --disable-muxers
  --disable-devices --disable-filters --disable-programs
  --disable-mediafoundation --disable-d3d11va --disable-d3d12va --disable-dxva2
  --enable-protocol=file
  --enable-demuxer=matroska,mov,avi,asf,mpegts,mp3,flac,ogg,wav,aac,ac3
  --enable-decoder=subrip,ass,ssa,movtext,webvtt,text            (#90 cues)
  --enable-decoder=aac,aac_latm,ac3,eac3,dca,truehd,mlp,flac,alac,opus,vorbis
  --enable-decoder=mp1,mp1float,mp2,mp2float,mp3,mp3float
  --enable-decoder=wmav1,wmav2,wmapro,wmalossless,amrnb,amrwb
  --enable-decoder=pcm_s16le,pcm_s16be,pcm_s24le,pcm_s24be,pcm_s32le,pcm_f32le
  --enable-decoder=pcm_f64le,pcm_u8,pcm_alaw,pcm_mulaw,pcm_bluray,pcm_dvd
  --enable-decoder=adpcm_ima_qt,adpcm_ms
  --enable-parser=h264,hevc,aac,aac_latm,ac3,dca,flac,opus,vorbis,mpegaudio
  --enable-parser=vp8,vp9,av1,mpeg4video,mpegvideo,vc1,webp,png,mjpeg
  --enable-bsf=extract_extradata,aac_adtstoasc,h264_mp4toannexb,hevc_mp4toannexb
  --enable-bsf=vp9_superframe,av1_frame_split,mpeg4_unpack_bframes,vp9_superframe_split

WHY THE AUDIO DECODERS ARE NOT OPTIONAL: they are never used to decode (MF does that). avformat_find_stream_info OPENS each audio codec to read its config, which is the only source of the NAMED channel layout. Without them ch_layout.order stays UNSPEC, layout_of() honestly returns None, and Details degrades to "6 channels" — i.e. straight back to MF's limitation. The list is deliberately keyed to the codecs tracks::audio_codec_display already knows how to name: we enable decoders for exactly the codecs we claim to describe.

Video decoders stay OUT — they are the bulk of avcodec (131.3 MB -> 23.25 MB .lib, measured 2026-07-14 from this exact committed recipe) and MF decodes everything. NOTE: an earlier note here claimed 9.8 MB; that was an OVER-trimmed intermediate from the stale-link detour below (before the audio decoders/parsers/bsfs were added back), not this recipe. The .lib is anyway a poor proxy — the linker drops what is never referenced, so a 23 MB .lib yields a +3.06 MB exe. --disable-network and --disable-mediafoundation also delete the objects that forced crypt32/ncrypt/mfuuid, so build.rs's link_ffmpeg_windows_syslibs is now belt-and-braces for the untrimmed case rather than load-bearing; it can be revisited once the overlay is the only supported build.

TWO TRAPS, both of which silently produce a WRONG build that still links and passes:
1. vcpkg classic mode only asks "is it installed?" — it does NOT re-evaluate a changed portfile. An overlay install after a plain install is a 235us no-op that silently keeps the OLD binary. `vcpkg remove ffmpeg:<triplet>` first (setup-libheif.ps1 already does exactly this for its libheif portfile patch).
2. Cargo does NOT relink when a vcpkg .lib changes: ffmpeg-sys-next emits no rerun-if-changed for the libs it links. Rebuilding FFmpeg and re-running `cargo test` with no source edit re-runs the PREVIOUSLY linked binary. This cost a real debugging detour here — three test runs 'failed' against a stale over-trimmed link and looked exactly like the trim breaking the layout. FIXED: build.rs::link_ffmpeg_windows_syslibs now emits rerun-if-changed for avcodec/avformat/avutil.lib, mirroring link_libheif_windows's heif.lib guard.

subtasks.title: LGPL: static-vs-dynamic decision, folded into #77
subtasks.description:
LGPL requires that users can relink against a modified library; a static link alone does not satisfy it — which is exactly #77 for libheif/libde265. Windows builds -static-md today. Decide: ship FFmpeg as DLLs (the clean, standard LGPL answer, and it sets the pattern that also fixes #77) vs static + published relink objects. The vcpkg crate takes VCPKGRS_DYNAMIC=1 for the dynamic triplet. Apply whatever is chosen to libheif/libde265 too — solving it once covers both. Add FFmpeg to THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and verify no --enable-gpl. Coordinate with #77 rather than duplicating it.

CONFIRMED during 100.1: FFmpeg's own configure output for this port reports `License: LGPL version 2.1 or later` — so the LGPL-2.1 assumption holds and the vcpkg gpl/x264/x265/nonfree features are all opt-in and off. The remaining question is purely static-vs-dynamic (the #77 relink story), not which licence applies.

=== RESOLVED 2026-07-14 (with #77, as intended). ===
Decision: DLLs, and it is implemented + green on x64. FFmpeg needed NO env var and NO VCPKGRS_DYNAMIC=1 in the end - dropping the `static` feature from pb-decode's ffmpeg-next dep makes ffmpeg-sys-next set that variable itself. Measured cost of the whole switch: +0.8 MB on-disk (exe 35.07 -> 29.04 MB plus 6.82 MB of DLLs), so the size objection died. FFmpeg is in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, --enable-gpl is confirmed off, and licenses/ffmpeg-COPYING.LGPLv2.1.txt now ships. See #77 for the full record and what is still open (arm64 unverified; no release cut yet).

subtasks.description:
scripts/setup-libheif.ps1 installs the ffmpeg port alongside libheif+dav1d, pinned to the same -VcpkgRef commit, for x64-windows-* AND arm64-windows-* (each on its NATIVE box — no cross toolchain is wired up). MEASURED during 100.1: (a) VCPKG_ROOT must be set in the build environment — the `vcpkg` crate that ffmpeg-sys-next uses has NO ~/vcpkg fallback, unlike our own build.rs. The release script + CI must export it. (b) vcpkg builds BOTH debug and release by default, which roughly doubles FFmpeg's wall clock and disk for a debug half we never ship. A custom triplet with `set(VCPKG_BUILD_TYPE release)` roughly halves both, and would apply to libheif/dav1d too — worth doing since releases are built locally on each native box (x64 AND arm64).

From 100.5: the overlay port (ports/ffmpeg + the patched portfile) must live in the repo and be installed by the setup script with an explicit `vcpkg remove ffmpeg:<triplet>` first — see trap 1 in subtask 5. The spike's overlay was built in a scratch dir and is NOT committed; regenerate it from the flag list recorded in subtask 5.

=== RESULT (2026-07-14): DONE for x64. ARM64 is WIRED BUT UNVERIFIED — no ARM64 box was available. ===
* setup-libheif.ps1 section 5 installs ffmpeg[core,avcodec,avformat,swresample,swscale]:$Triplet from the SAME pinned -VcpkgRef tree, patching ports/ffmpeg/portfile.cmake IN PLACE at the OPTIONS anchor (idempotency marker 'PhotoBlaze task #100', `vcpkg remove` first per trap 1, throw if the upstream anchor moved). NOT a committed overlay dir as 100.5 assumed: patching the pinned tree is what the script ALREADY does for libheif, so it reuses the proven pattern instead of adding a second mechanism.
* PROVEN END-TO-END on the real tree (not the spike's scratch overlay): script run clean, exit 0, portfile marker present, 6 min, libs rebuilt trimmed — avcodec.lib 23.25 MB (vs 131.3 MB untrimmed), avformat 7.79, avutil 6.80. Script verifies all four of heif/dav1d/avcodec/avformat and warns if avcodec.lib > 40 MB (a stale untrimmed build that would otherwise link fine and just be fat).
* Ship feature set is now --features libheif,dav1d,ffprobe in release-windows.ps1 (build + the throw message) and in CI (both lanes). CI's "already present?" guard now checks avcodec.lib TOO, not just heif+dav1d — a runner provisioned before #100 has heif+dav1d, so a heif-only guard would skip setup and then fail the build.
* NEW BUILD-ENV REQUIREMENT, now handled: ffprobe is the first feature needing a VS *Developer shell* (bindgen's clang reads INCLUDE for stdint.h; a plain cargo build never did). New scripts/vs-dev-env.ps1 finds+validates the install, enters the shell, sets LIBCLANG_PATH, and exports to $GITHUB_ENV under Actions; release-windows.ps1 and both CI lanes call it (skipped if already in a dev shell).
  TRAP found by running it: the copy-pasted `vswhere -latest -products *` returns SQL SERVER MANAGEMENT STUDIO on this box — SSMS is built on the VS shell so it matches, and has no C++ tools; the failure is a baffling "DevShell.dll module not found". The helper requires a VC-tools component AND verifies DevShell.dll + libclang.dll exist before trusting an install.
* NOT DONE (deliberate): (a) no rename to setup-native-libs.ps1 — dav1d was added under the old name too, and a rename churns CLAUDE.md + CI + release script + docs for no functional gain; (b) VCPKG_BUILD_TYPE=release custom triplet (the 100.1 idea to skip vcpkg's debug half) not pursued — it is a separate win that applies to libheif/dav1d equally and belongs in its own task, not folded into a feature landing; (c) Setup.exe delta not re-measured — the exe delta is measured (see #100 description), and the installer number needs a real signed release run.
* ARM64: the vcpkg ffmpeg port building cleanly on arm64-windows-static-md is a GENUINE UNKNOWN (assembly + runtime cpu-detect have arm64 history). The arm64 CI lane is wired to prove it and its comment says so; if the port fails there, that is the finding.

subtasks.title: Reconcile #90's Windows path
subtasks.description:
With demux available, revisit #90 (deps 79/84/98): its text tier is SubRip (.srt sidecar), MP4 mov_text/tx3g and WebVTT, decoded through the FFmpeg backend. Confirm the cue path rides this same FFmpeg on Windows (subtitle decoders from subtask 5) and update #90/#99 to say so — today they silently assume a backend Windows does not have.

=== RECONCILED 2026-07-14. Half of #90's text tier works on Windows; the sidecar half does NOT. ===
Verified against what the trimmed vcpkg FFmpeg ACTUALLY built (vcpkg buildtrees/ffmpeg/
build-x64-windows-rel-out.log, not the portfile's intent):

  Enabled demuxers (11): aac ac3 asf avi flac matroska mov mp3 mpegts ogg wav
  Enabled subtitle decoders (6): ass movtext ssa subrip text webvtt

So, for #90's three text sources:
  * MP4 mov_text/tx3g  -> WORKS  (mov demuxer + movtext decoder both present)
  * MKV subrip/ass/webvtt -> WORKS  (matroska demuxer + the decoders present)
  * A STANDALONE .srt / .vtt / .ass SIDECAR -> DOES NOT WORK. Opening a sidecar as its own file
    needs the `srt` / `webvtt` / `ass` DEMUXER, and the #100.5 trim enables none of them. A decoder
    cannot open a file; it only turns packets into cues. This is a gap the trim introduced, not a
    pre-existing FFmpeg limitation.

That matters because #90.1 already ships `MediaTrack::external` specifically to mark sidecar tracks,
so sidecars are in the design, and Windows is the one platform whose FFmpeg is deliberately trimmed
(Linux/macOS link a full build and are unaffected).

TWO WAYS OUT - #90's call, deliberately NOT decided here:
  (a) Add `--enable-demuxer=srt,webvtt,ass` to the trim in scripts/setup-libheif.ps1. These are
      plain text parsers, so the size cost should be negligible - but it means rebuilding the vcpkg
      port, re-measuring the +3.06 MB figure, and redoing it per arch.
  (b) Parse sidecars in pure Rust and keep FFmpeg for in-container cues only. SRT/WebVTT are trivial
      line-based text formats; this costs no FFmpeg change, no size, no arm64 rebuild, and matches
      the project's preference for pure Rust where it is cheap (ADR-015). Probably the better fit,
      since Windows FFmpeg exists ONLY to read container track tables.
Do not discover this from a runtime failure - decide it before #90.2 wires the cue path.
